=== origin git@gitlab.com:o/proj.git: setup proj --yes
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: paths.origin git@gitlab.com:o/proj.git: gitlab.com is not GitHub. A forge without GitHub's deploy keys gets no platform push (and an ssh alias isn't read: the push reads no ssh config); push it yourself with brunna push --owner

=== origin /srv/git/proj.git: setup proj --yes
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: paths.origin /srv/git/proj.git is not a GitHub remote: the platform pushes only to GitHub, through a deploy key (no other forge, no local path)

=== public, nobody answering: none and the to-do: setup proj --yes

--- stdout

--- stderr

=== the key doesn't work: setup proj --yes --branches all
[exit 1]
--- stdout
The remote is public. On a public remote every branch you allow is published as soon as it is pushed, and a site or deploy that builds from branches (gh-pages, a hosting 'production branch', preview deploys) runs it. 'others' keeps the default branch's CI and deploys yours, not the content private.
To push proj's branches, the platform will use your gh login (octo) on github.com/o/proj to add a deploy key with WRITE access to that repo. The key can write only that repo, nothing else of your account. A deploy key titled "brunna push: proj" that the platform added there before is replaced.
The platform keeps the private key in its secrets folder (not in the cloud backup) and uses it only to push the branches of proj that its sessions ask for, after the automatic checks.
To undo it: brunna push setup proj --revoke (deletes the key at GitHub and here).
Going ahead: the branches were given on the command line, which counts as your yes.
--- stderr
failed: the new deploy key didn't work (GitHub refused the deploy key (it was removed, or gh's sign-in that added it was revoked)); it was removed again

=== interactive, no to the key: setup proj
[exit 2]
--- stdout
The remote is private. On a public remote every branch you allow is published as soon as it is pushed, and a site or deploy that builds from branches (gh-pages, a hosting 'production branch', preview deploys) runs it. 'others' keeps the default branch's CI and deploys yours, not the content private.
Which branches may the platform push for proj? none: you push yourself; others: every branch but the default; all: the default branch too. others and all add a deploy key with write access to the repo with your gh login: you are told what that does and asked first.
none, others or all? [all] all
To push proj's branches, the platform will use your gh login (octo) on github.com/o/proj to add a deploy key with WRITE access to that repo. The key can write only that repo, nothing else of your account. A deploy key titled "brunna push: proj" that the platform added there before is replaced.
The platform keeps the private key in its secrets folder (not in the cloud backup) and uses it only to push the branches of proj that its sessions ask for, after the automatic checks.
To undo it: brunna push setup proj --revoke (deletes the key at GitHub and here).
Add the deploy key with your gh login? [y/N] n
You said no: no deploy key was added for proj, and nothing was changed. brunna push setup proj asks again whenever you want it.
